story: 11th Airborne Division paratroopers fly armed FPV drones in the first kinetic drone strike in the Richardson Training Area, and soldiers pitch drone fixes at the Angel Ascent innovation competition

claims.claim: Paratroopers of the 2nd Mobile Brigade Combat Team (Airborne), 11th Airborne Division, conducted multi-purpose company live-fire exercises in Alaska.
claims.verbatim: Paratroopers assigned to the 2nd Mobile Brigade Combat Team (Airborne), 11th Airborne Division
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews
claims.notes: Dateline Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson. AI CHECK: none of AI, artificial intelligence, autonomy, autonomous or machine learning appears in this article, nor in 296502, 296265 or the Army Recognition body text.

claims.claim: The live-fire exercises took place on September 29th and October 19th to 20th.
claims.verbatim: on Sept. 29 and Oct. 19-20, 2026
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews
claims.notes: Events predate the window; the Army's report (October 27th) is inside it. Corroborated by Army Recognition.

claims.claim: The exercises were held at the Multi-Purpose Training Range in the Richardson Training Area.
claims.verbatim: at the Multi-Purpose Training Range (MPTR) in the Richardson Training Area
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews
claims.notes: The body does not say the Richardson Training Area is part of JBER; only the dateline names JBER.

claims.claim: The exercises included the first kinetic drone strike conducted within the Richardson Training Area.
claims.verbatim: including the first kinetic drone strike conducted within the Richardson Training Area.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews
claims.notes: Scope is the Richardson Training Area only. Corroborated by Army Recognition.

claims.claim: The strike used armed first-person view drones.
claims.verbatim: armed first-person view (FPV) drones
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews
claims.notes: No model, maker, weight, range or cost given.

claims.claim: The exercises integrated armed small unmanned aircraft systems, sniper teams, reconnaissance elements and a gun truck.
claims.value: sniper teams, reconnaissance elements and a gun truck
claims.verbatim: integrated armed small unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS), sniper teams, reconnaissance elements and a gun truck
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews

claims.claim: Before the live strikes, operators flew test flights with unarmed explosive payloads to see how the added weight affected maneuverability.
claims.verbatim: These flights allowed operators to evaluate how the additional weight affected aircraft maneuverability
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews
claims.notes: Earlier sentence: 'enabled operators to conduct test flights with unarmed explosive payloads'. No payload weight figure stated.

claims.claim: Sgt. 1st Class Devin McNamara, the brigade's sUAS master trainer, helped enable the test flights.
claims.verbatim: sUAS master trainer, Sgt. 1st Class Devin McNamara, enabled operators to conduct test flights
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews

claims.claim: The brigade's Multi-Functional Reconnaissance Company, commanded by Capt. Pat Robinson, coordinated the initial effort and flew the first live strike.
claims.verbatim: Multi-Functional Reconnaissance Company, commanded by Capt. Pat Robinson, coordinated the initial effort
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews
claims.notes: First live flight and strike from Capt. Bartoli's quote, 'The MFRC executed the first live flight and strike'.

claims.claim: Capt. Raymond Bartoli, a brigade planner and officer in charge of the live-fire range, said "The Kinetic Drone Strike completed on MPTR was the first of its kind in the Richardson Training Area (RTA)."
claims.verbatim: The Kinetic Drone Strike completed on MPTR was the first of its kind in the Richardson Training Area (RTA)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews

claims.claim: The Army article says these drone capabilities are particularly relevant to the Spartan Brigade in Arctic and mountainous environments.
claims.verbatim: For the Spartan Brigade, these capabilities are particularly relevant in Arctic and mountainous environments,
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Correy Mathews
claims.notes: Army's own framing; attribute it.

claims.claim: Army Recognition reported that the Army did not identify the drone model, payload mass, flight endurance, engagement range or measured accuracy.
claims.value: no model, payload mass or range disclosed
claims.verbatim: does not identify the drone model, payload mass, flight endurance, engagement range, or measured accuracy
claims.source_outlet: Army Recognition, by Alain Servaes
claims.notes: Matches the fact-checker's own reading of 296380.

claims.claim: Army Recognition cautioned that the Richardson strike should not be read as the Army's first use of an explosive FPV drone.
claims.verbatim: should not be interpreted as the Army
claims.source_outlet: Army Recognition, by Alain Servaes
claims.notes: Army Recognition's analysis, not the Army's statement. Hedge as according to Army Recognition.

claims.claim: The 11th Airborne Division held its Angel Ascent innovation competition on October 28th at the division theater.
claims.verbatim: demonstrated the power of grassroots innovation during Angel Ascent, held Oct. 28 at the division theater.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: Dateline Fort Wainwright, Alaska. AI CHECK: none of the AI terms appear.

claims.claim: Spc. Leighton Keilen of 1st Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment, 1st Infantry Brigade Combat Team, won first place at Angel Ascent.
claims.verbatim: Spc. Leighton Keilen, 1st Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment, 1st Infantry Brigade Combat Team, 11th Airborne Division
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: 'earned first place for his Skydio Drone Relay and modular payload delivery system'.

claims.claim: Keilen's winning entry was a Skydio drone relay and modular payload delivery system.
claims.verbatim: earned first place for his Skydio Drone Relay and modular payload delivery system
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: No range, distance or payload weight given.

claims.claim: The Army says Keilen's system significantly extends tactical drone range and utility in Alaska's rugged, mountainous terrain.
claims.verbatim: significantly extends tactical drone range and utility in Alaska
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: Unquantified; attribute to the Army.

claims.claim: Col. Matthew Adamczyk presented Keilen with a Meritorious Service Medal.
claims.verbatim: Col. Matthew Adamczyk presented Keilen with a Meritorious Service Medal.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: Adamczyk is deputy commanding officer for operations, 11th Airborne Division.

claims.claim: Every other Angel Ascent competitor received an Army Commendation Medal, and every participant got a four-day pass.
claims.verbatim: All other competitors received Army Commendation Medals, and every participant was awarded a four-day pass
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: No count of competitors given.

claims.claim: Each innovator had 10 minutes to brief a project, followed by five minutes of questions from the judges.
claims.value: 10 minutes plus five minutes of questions
claims.verbatim: Each innovator received 10 minutes to brief their project followed by five minutes of questions from the judging panel
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith

claims.claim: Judges scored entries on problem identification, solution quality, operational value, resource requirements and presentation.
claims.verbatim: evaluated entries on problem identification, solution quality, operational value, resource requirements and presentation
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith

claims.claim: Pfc. Michael Pereira hand-sewed a prototype passive thermal battery vault to keep drone batteries working in sub-zero temperatures using only body heat and radiant barriers.
claims.verbatim: passive thermal battery vault designed to keep drone batteries viable in sub-zero temperatures using only body heat and radiant barriers
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: No temperature figure given. 'hand-sewed his first prototype' on the page.

claims.claim: Other Angel Ascent entries included 3D-printed explosively formed penetrators for FPV drones.
claims.verbatim: 3D-printed explosively formed penetrators for FPV drones
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: Also listed: 'a low-cost battery eliminator for PRC-158 radios in extreme cold' and 'a modular power and heating system for man-hauled Ahkio sleds'.

claims.claim: Another entry was a unit-fabricated ring mount hatch for FMTVs that protects convoy gunners in Arctic conditions.
claims.verbatim: a unit-fabricated ring mount hatch for FMTVs that protects convoy gunners in Arctic conditions
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: Probably the 725th LSB entry in 296265, not confirmed.

claims.claim: Col. Matthew Adamczyk said "Soldiers across the 11th Airborne Division continue to demonstrate that many of the best ideas come from the bottom up."
claims.verbatim: Soldiers across the 11th Airborne Division continue to demonstrate that many of the best ideas come from the bottom up.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith

claims.claim: Staff Sgt. Robert Baddeley developed TroopToTask.org, a platform that combines personnel, training and duty data for leaders.
claims.verbatim: Staff Sgt. Baddeley, a respiratory therapist from Petaluma, California, developed TroopToTask.org
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Capt. Luke Smith
claims.notes: Description paraphrased.

claims.claim: Angel Ascent is the 11th Airborne Division's twice-yearly innovation competition, sponsored by the division's Innovations Lab.
claims.verbatim: bi-annual service-member innovation competition
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Master Sgt. Adam Ross
claims.notes: Background; preview before the window.

claims.claim: The October 28th competition was the second iteration of Angel Ascent.
claims.verbatim: The second iteration of Angel Ascent will bring multiple teams of creative thinkers together
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Master Sgt. Adam Ross
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: A team from the 725th Light Support Battalion, 2nd Mobile Brigade Combat Team (Airborne), designed a metal replacement for the soft cloth gunner hatch covers on Light Medium Tactical Vehicles, which let snow leak into the cab.
claims.verbatim: this feature often led to snow leaking into the cabin of the vehicle
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Master Sgt. Adam Ross
claims.notes: Team led by Capt. Daniel Woodard; 'simple 3-d design software'.

claims.claim: Other units can reproduce the metal hatch cover for roughly $300 in materials.
claims.verbatim: can now be reproduced by other units for roughly $300 of materials
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Master Sgt. Adam Ross
claims.notes: Only cost figure in the three Army articles; a hatch cover, not a drone.

claims.claim: Capt. Daniel Woodard said "We put together a metal version that can sustain the weight of snow, and can also be popped open easily."
claims.verbatim: We put together a metal version that can sustain the weight of snow, and can also be popped open easily
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Master Sgt. Adam Ross

claims.claim: Capt. Eleanor Manning, deputy of innovations at the 11th Airborne Division Innovations Lab, said "The overall intent is not to just select one winner."
claims.verbatim: The overall intent is not to just select one winner
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Army (army.mil), by Master Sgt. Adam Ross
claims.notes: Another Manning quote: 'A lot of these Soldiers are going out and buying printers and other technology on their own dime'.

claims.claim: Enstar Natural Gas applied to the Regulatory Commission of Alaska to approve a proposed gas exchange with Matanuska Electric Association.
claims.verbatim: Enstar Natural Gas Co. has applied to the Regulatory Commission of Alaska for approval of a proposed natural gas exchange
claims.source_outlet: Petroleum News, by Alan Bailey
claims.notes: Runner-up story.

claims.claim: MEA, Enstar and Hilcorp signed a gas exchange agreement covering 1.2 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
claims.verbatim: a gas exchange agreement involving 1.2 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
claims.source_outlet: Matanuska Electric Association
claims.notes: Runner-up story.

claims.claim: Enstar is to return equivalent gas volumes to MEA no later than March 31st, 2028.
claims.verbatim: ENSTAR will return equivalent gas volumes to MEA no later than March 31, 2028.
claims.source_outlet: Matanuska Electric Association
claims.notes: Runner-up story.

claims.claim: MEA estimates the exchange will save its members about $2 million, subject to regulatory approval.
claims.verbatim: providing approximately $2 million in estimated savings for MEA members, subject to regulatory approval and implementation.
claims.source_outlet: Matanuska Electric Association
claims.notes: Runner-up story; interested-party projection.

claims.claim: MEA CEO Tony Izzo said "This agreement demonstrates how utilities can work together to address regional energy challenges."
claims.verbatim: This agreement demonstrates how utilities can work together to address regional energy challenges
claims.source_outlet: Matanuska Electric Association
claims.notes: Runner-up story.

claims.claim: Enstar asked the RCA for an expedited decision on the exchange.
claims.verbatim: Enstar is asking the commission for an expedited decision
claims.source_outlet: Petroleum News, by Alan Bailey
claims.notes: Runner-up story.

claims.claim: With 98 percent of precincts reporting on election night, Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins led the governor's race with 49 percent of the vote.
claims.verbatim: With 98% of precincts reporting, Kreiss-Tomkins leads with 49% of the vote.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media, by Eric Stone
claims.notes: Runner-up story; unofficial first-choice results.

claims.claim: Republican Bernadette Wilson was second with about 29 percent of first-choice votes.
claims.verbatim: business owner Bernadette Wilson is in second with 29%
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media, by Eric Stone
claims.notes: Runner-up story.

claims.claim: Ranked-choice ballots in the governor's race are to be tabulated on November 18th.
claims.verbatim: when election officials tally ranked choice ballots Nov. 18.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media, by Eric Stone
claims.notes: Runner-up story.

claims.claim: Kreiss-Tomkins told the Alaska Beacon he supports a moratorium on data center development in Alaska until the Legislature passes a regulatory framework.
claims.verbatim: I support a moratorium on data center development in Alaska
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, by James Brooks (via Alaska Public Media)
claims.notes: Runner-up story; background.

claims.claim: Wilson said she would never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers.
claims.verbatim: I will never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers that take our resources and spoil our lands.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon, by James Brooks (via Alaska Public Media)
claims.notes: Runner-up story; background.

killed.claim: army.mil 296502 calls Angel Ascent the second iteration of a bi-annual competition.
killed.why: Those phrases are only in the October 21st preview (C27, C28).

killed.claim: The Richardson Training Area is on JBER.
killed.why: No fetched page states it; 296380 has only a JBER dateline.

killed.claim: Any range, weight, endurance, temperature or cost figure for the FPV drones or the relay.
killed.why: None exists in any fetched article (C12).

killed.claim: Angel Ascent soldiers presented to division leaders.
killed.why: Page says senior military leaders, civilian officials and innovation experts.

killed.claim: Background facts on 2nd MBCT or the 11th Airborne Division.
killed.why: No fetched page states any beyond unit names and the Spartan Brigade nickname.

killed.why: Each single-sourced to Petroleum News; the RCA filing is unreachable.

killed.claim: Bronson 14 percent, Taylor 7 percent; 216,000 counted; noon December 7th inauguration.
killed.why: Single article each; Division of Elections returned 503.
